summary:
Deep Frontier is an interactive space exploration game designed to make learning about space science and engineering fun, simple, and engaging. Instead of just reading about space missions, players get to experience what it takes to plan and complete one themselves.

The game allows players to explore three fascinating destinations: Titan, the Moon, and Mars. They can design their own spacecraft, choose equipment, manage resources like power and budget, and launch missions into space. Along the way, players face exciting challenges, conduct scientific experiments, and discover interesting facts about different worlds.

Using scientific concepts and resources from NASA, the game combines education with adventure, helping players understand how real space missions work. It also encourages creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving through hands-on experiences.

Our goal is to make space exploration more accessible and enjoyable, especially for younger learners, while inspiring curiosity about the universe and the possibilities of future space exploration
details:
Deep Frontier is an interactive educational space exploration game designed to make space science and engineering fun, engaging, and accessible, especially for younger learners. Instead of simply reading about space missions, players get to experience the challenges of planning and completing one themselves.

Players choose between three destinations: Titan, the Moon, and Mars. They design spacecraft by selecting rockets, power systems, and scientific instruments while managing resources such as mass, power, and budget. After launching, players experience animated space travel, explore planetary environments, conduct scientific experiments, and collect discoveries.

Our project combines education with entertainment, helping players develop critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills while learning about real scientific concepts.

We developed the game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Canvas and SVG for animations and planetary environments. We also used Node.js for local hosting and testing, along with NASA's Image and Video Library and Planetary Data System for authentic scientific resources.

What makes our project unique is its combination of spacecraft customization, interactive exploration, and hands-on experiments. Players can investigate Titan's lakes, perform lunar laser experiments, and explore Martian geology.

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific accuracy, simplicity, accessibility, and engaging gameplay, ensuring that younger players could understand the concepts without feeling overwhelmed.

Our ultimate goal is to make space exploration more approachable and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers through interactive learning.

Note: The game is compatible only for Laptops and Monitors
